assumptions: The connected GitHub repository holds the landing page copy the product's visitors read.
Public threads about the product exist on at least one chosen platform within the window; when they do not, insufficient data is the correct result.
A copy fix cannot be measured until it is merged and deployed, and only affects visitors after that.
effects: Opens one unmerged GitHub pull request of at most three files, or none for a report-only or insufficient-data result.
Writes the receipt reports/feedback-to-fix/{run_id}/RESULT.md in this project.
cost_drivers: The number of threads and comments opened, which grows with the window and platforms chosen.
Running the repository's own lint and test commands.

rubric.question: Is every quote exactly what the page says, with a link to the comment or thread it was read in?
Does every theme the report acts on have at least two different people behind it, counted from the quotes?
Does the report and the pull request avoid usernames and put no one's words on the site?
Does every changed sentence say only what the Feature map or the code shows the product does?

cases.description: Two launch threads where different people say the first screen is confusing and ask what to start with; the repository has a hero section and a first-run screen.
Boundary: a single commenter raises three separate points across a thread. One person is not a theme, so nothing changes.
Plausible but unusable input: the chosen platform cannot be opened at all. It must say so and must not fill the report from memory.
